[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Nested snippet sessions in the prompt input widget[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]Expanding a snippet while another snippet's tabstops are still [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]pending suspends the outer snippet instead of destroying it: the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]nested snippet's tabstops are visited first, and once they are [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]exhausted `Tab` resumes the enclosing snippet at the stop after the[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]one that was nested into. Tabstop anchors survive arbitrary editing[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]because they are remapped from real document deltas, `Shift+Tab` [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]steps backwards through the visited stops, and the whole session [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]state machine lives in the Rust core so any future frontend gets [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]the same behavior.[/#D7D7AF]
